texts.preamble: Tabish Khan Ziauddin Khan vs The State Of Maharashtra on 9 January, 2026 2026:Bhc-Aug:754 955 Ba No.2464.2025 -1- In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Bail Application No. 2464 Of 2025 Tabish Khan Ziauddin Khan Versus The State Of Maharashtra ** * Advocate for Applicant : Mr. Satej S. Jadhav App for Respondents-State : Mr. C. V. Bhadane ** * Coram : Sachin S. Deshmukh, J. Date : 9th January, 2026 Order :
texts.facts: - 1. The applicant has approached this Court seeking regular bail in connection with FIR dated 26.11.2025 bearing Crime No. 511 of 2025 registered with Satara Police Station, Dist. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for the offences punishable under Sections 123, 223, 274, 275 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Sections 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act. 2. The prosecution's case is that on 26.11.2025, the Food Safety Officer / informant received credible intelligence that the accused / applicant, in Plot No. 5, Martand Nagar, Satara Parisar, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, had stored illegal banned food substance. The authorities raided the said place and seized the contraband amounting worth Rs. 36,06,178/- under a panchanama. Consequently, the FIR came to be lodged.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the crime. The allegations pertain to regulatory offences under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and there is no material to show that he manufactured, sold or stored any unsafe food products. It is further submitted that the provisions of Section 123 of the BNS are not applicable against the applicant. The investigation is almost complete and the alleged substance is recovered by the Tabish Khan Ziauddin Khan vs The State Of Maharashtra on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69864943/ 1 investigating agency. Hence, further incarceration of the applicant is unjustified and prayed to allow the application. 4. The learned APP opposed the application, submitting that the accused was apprehended as the driver of the vehicle carrying the banned substance of tobacco, while three associates fled from the spot. Given the serious nature of the offense, it is contended that the applicant's release on bail would pose a significant risk of tampering with evidence. Consequently, the prayed for the application to be rejected.
